questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic, career and studying in an international environment. Also what the grade average was for applying and the ranking of the university was less important but still a crucial aspect.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the best study experience i could have asked for.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the WUR portal helps you a lot and there are always people at Wageningen you can ask.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was part of the introduction days, where all the assistance i need was.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's wasn't quite "on campus" but there are many student housing in Wageningen connected to WUR. You could apply for al kinds of housing. Only hared bathroom or with shared kitchen, or just completely self contained housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Depend on what student housing you will end with. Generally many have shared kitchen some have a kitchenette you need to buy a cooker for. But all Idealis student housing for WUR contains the most you need. Meal plans nothing but relatively low priced food option on campus and in the university building. Otherwise a very close nearby supermarked.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You might wan't too adjust something in your room or acquire all the different unite cooking things you want before starting your studies. Not everything will be there if you lived in no shared kitchen or self-contained. But many option for this, many student will sell their thing when leaving and there are some great thrift store where you can find most.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a really nice room and they changed all the furniture while i was there, big bed, nice wardrobe and so on. But you can be unlucky with the hall mates or housemate you have. So be aware that not everyone has the same experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was kind of confused with all the documentations i needed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied through my own universities exchange portal, after that i was registered at the university and didn't need to do much. I was sent all the information on email by the erasmus exchange coordinator in Wageningen for the university portal and my student email.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus coordinator and student in wageningen.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can seem confusing at first, but if you understand the structure of their periods and time of day for the courses it's not hard. So when applying remember to look for a MO (morning course) and AF(afternoon) course if you need to have two courses in one period. Some courses also run the whole day (WO) for certain period where you can only manage one course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super nice academic programmes, since i was on exchange i just took different courses i was interested in. But i am amazed with the option they have and this made me consider taking my master at WUR.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took mainly BA course and one MA course. But most of them were full of different background for both master and bachelor. Level is high, you need to study a lot so be prepared.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most was the same, but wur really puts a lot effort into group work so there is much opportunity to challenge yourself and exersize your communication skills on a high academic level.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biofunctional Food Ingredients (FCH38306)
Cell Biology and Health (CBI20306)
Food Related Allergies and Intolerances (FCH21806)
Food Microbiology (FHM20306)
Nutrition and Cancer (HNH37806)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: it's hard to recommend a specific because it depend on your interest. I just recommend you to take what you find interesting and relevant for your future work, skills, study.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buy kitchen stuff, i had a non-shared kitchen. But even the cooker i needed to buy be aware.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands are very compatible with Danish prices so i was not shocked.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many association to choose from, both academic, social and sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything, you can really find a lot and if you join introduction days there will be a market where you can meet a bunch of them!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joint the ESN (Erasmus student Network) when you arrive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel the netherlands and world. So many flix-bus options, many cities to see in the netherlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, go talk and join social events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non, very much same as Danish.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It was a very internation environment so i didn't dive a lot into the dutch culture. I wasn't interested in this aspect. But i appreciated that i got to learn so much from so many cultures all over the world.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to study a lot, they have a different exams forms than what i was used too. 
Not everyone is equally good at speaking english. 
Be social, meet lot's of different cultures and people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Wageningen is a very small city, but you will be busy when you make new friends. Also there is a whole sport center, so lot's of opportunity to explore different sports.
When looking for housing there is a very good facebook group to join "Wageningen Student Plaza" i strongly recommend to join it even if you find housing through their official portal "
Idealis.nl
" and "
room.nl
".

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The friends and people i met. 
The experience of another university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The exam form the opperate with. 
I was not used to "learn-by-heart" and mostly multiple choice exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
You have great opportunity to change the courses when you are there if you et in doubt or choose something you figure out you don't really want to take. 
Remember to check if your student housing offers subsidy, this means you can get some money back from the rent you pay.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
